mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to potential monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, which in turn negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 1 month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals increased demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment reacts to potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases > 1% MoM, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% year-over-year, it indicates a potential mismatch between monetary policy and inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals increased consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS increases for 3 consecutive months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a contraction in supply and a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases and UNRATE increases, the hypothesis is rejected.
